references.title: B-wing starfighter

notes.lesson: Build a distinctive asymmetric starfighter around a narrow spine and separate wing masses.
notes.construction: Study cockpit mass, long blade, smaller side wings, engine block and detailed wing ends as separate design roles.
notes.interfaces: Preserve wing-root and engine attachments; the model is delivered in its source pose, with no claim of working articulation.
notes.parent_context: Full model includes the supplied parent assembly.
notes.reuse_notes: Adapt the silhouette and module interfaces deliberately; keep real canopy, engine and wing parts rather than replacing their forms with rectangular slabs.

discovery.description: Complete B-Wing starfighter assembled from its wing, fuselage, and engine submodels.

references.repair_reason: Resolve tiny rounded-coordinate body-envelope penetrations in the posed wing plate/tile stack; maximum displacement is under 0.00033 LDU. Part identity, colour and orientation are unchanged. Strict collision tolerances remain unchanged.

references.title: UCS Y-wing: proportions and engine detailing

notes.lesson: Use a long spine and paired nacelles to create an immediately readable heavy starfighter.
notes.construction: Study the rounded forward cockpit, exposed machinery, outriggers and repeated engine ribs against quieter hull surfaces.
notes.interfaces: Engine outriggers and display stand need their own support study before reuse.
notes.parent_context: This is a whole-set reference including its stand; source geometry diagnostics are retained.
notes.reuse_notes: Inspiration only: repair or rebuild selected modules before using them. The greebled machinery and curved/angled assemblies need more than a matching BOM.

discovery.description: LEGO Star Wars Ultimate Collector Series Y-wing Attack Starfighter (set 10134-1): a Rebel starfighter with a long central fuselage, a tinted bubble cockpit with twin nose laser cannons and an R5-D4 astromech droid, two large ribbed engine nacelles on outrigger struts, and a dorsal sensor/ion-cannon turret, presented on a black display stand with a tiled info plaque

references.title: Imperial Star Destroyer: layered wedge hull

notes.lesson: Layer a broad wedge hull, narrow edge trenches and smaller superstructure to establish capital-ship scale.
notes.construction: Compare upper and lower panel thickness, perimeter recesses, bridge silhouette and engine cluster.
notes.interfaces: Long hull panels require real hinge/brace interfaces and an internal frame; a visually aligned wedge does not establish an attachment.
notes.parent_context: This is the full source assembly; source transform and overlap errors remain visible.
notes.reuse_notes: Inspiration only: do not export it as a checked construction. Rebuild useful panel techniques with proper rigid placements and inspect the internal support structure.

discovery.description: Assembly of a large wedge-shaped Imperial Star Destroyer built from layered grey plates, angled wing sections, and click-lock hinge mechanisms.

notes.lesson: A long spacecraft wing can carry an engine pod and a slender tip feature while retaining a layered, readable silhouette.
notes.construction: Read the plate sandwich, local bracing, nacelle and tip assembly as linked submodels. Whole-section views are supplied; prepare its source sections separately for build pages.
notes.interfaces: Retain the source wing-root stack and inspect the exact mating parts before attaching it to a new spine.
notes.parent_context: 7191-1.mpd supplies the other wings, central fuselage and wing articulation. This is one lower port wing, not a mirrored pair.
notes.reuse_notes: Use a real opposite-hand construction or rebuild it with matching left/right parts; never mirror physical part matrices. Keep the nacelle and long projecting details clear of neighbouring wings.

discovery.description: The lower port X-wing wing assembly built from wing panels, long plates, and grooved tiles forming the layered attack-wing surface.

notes.lesson: Use genuine cylinders and concentric round parts to give an engine a convincing layered profile.
notes.construction: A single source STEP group combines the cylindrical shell, red round inner pieces and axle core. Read the part list because there are no intermediate insertions in the source.
notes.interfaces: Keep the coaxial core and cylinder spacing; inspect its parent mounting shaft and the full pod envelope.
notes.parent_context: 7191-1.mpd supplies the surrounding wing and fore/aft engine context.
notes.reuse_notes: Change external mounts and hull palette carefully while preserving the concentric stack and dedicated engine shapes.

discovery.description: Cylindrical engine nacelle using Technic cylinders, round red bricks, and axle-connected structural components.

notes.lesson: Design the cockpit envelope around real canopy halves and hinges before closing the hull.
notes.construction: The cockpit combines two octagonal transparent canopy halves, hinge fingers, a glazed rear panel, side mounts and a pilot subassembly. Read the child pages for its layers and occupant.
notes.interfaces: Retain mating canopy hinges and the panel rim; inspect source mounting bricks and their exact orientation before attaching to a new fuselage.
notes.parent_context: 6887-1.mpd (Allied Avenger) supplies the surrounding spacecraft and mating rear structure. The extraction includes its pilot and several legacy part aliases.
notes.reuse_notes: Use the enclosure and hinge vocabulary in a new cockpit. Preserve the clear opening and actual pilot envelope; any new seat, controls or canopy substitution needs its own fit review.

notes.lesson: Combine sloped armour with a small raised vent cluster and a deliberate hinge edge.
notes.construction: Read the layered wedge plates, curved/sloped surface and concentrated grille details in successive steps.
notes.interfaces: Preserve the underlying plate bond and hinge mating face; measure the panel envelope before installing it over machinery.
notes.parent_context: 75181-1.mpd supplies the rest of the Y-wing hull and the mating panel supports.
notes.reuse_notes: Adapt a matched set of panels, retaining clean outer surfaces beside a few dense service areas. Use actual left/right pieces for handed variants.

discovery.description: Angled hull armor panel built from plates, slope bricks, raised grille plates, and a hinge tile forming a contoured body panel with greebled detailing.

notes.lesson: Small familiar LEGO fittings can suggest machinery when arranged in a coherent recessed service bay.
notes.construction: Study the domes, control sticks, loudhailer, antenna and wing panel as a small directed composition.
notes.interfaces: Reserve the protruding antenna and bar envelope; attach the underlying plate to exposed studs, not through finished hull tiles.
notes.parent_context: 10179-1.mpd supplies the surrounding hull recess. This is the right upper service cluster, not an entire Falcon panel.
notes.reuse_notes: Keep greebles grouped and lower than the main silhouette. Reuse their mounting logic; avoid covering every hull surface with unrelated decoration.

discovery.description: Upper hull greeble cluster (right): wing panel, domes, control sticks, loudhailer and antenna
